lens: Day 3 verify round 3: does the emitted pyto-run-record@1 satisfy every claim in pyto/viewer/RECORD.md, do the hard rules hold, and does the build report describe the tree that exists?

findings.claim: RECORD.md's field rule says "`inputs` keeps the testimony spelling: `px:<address>` for a Part binding, `fn:<id>` for a result binding. `declared_consumes` repeats them in binding order." That claim does not hold of the record this build emits: 13 of the 15 invocations have `fn:` bindings in `inputs` and an EMPTY `declared_consumes`.
findings.evidence: From /home/user/DiscStudio-staging/pyto/experiments/grouped-ablation/evidence/run-1/record.json: fit.all has inputs {'split': 'fn:split'} and declared_consumes []; score.all has inputs {'model': 'fn:fit.all', 'split': 'fn:split'} and declared_consumes []; compare has six fn: inputs and declared_consumes []. Only split and select (px: bindings) satisfy the sentence. The cause is materialize.py:416 `declared_consumes = [f"px:{address}" for address in receipt.declared_consumes]`, and pcr.py:120 Receipt.declared_consumes carries Part reads only. Both readers already know the doc is wrong and work around it in code rather than the spec: viewer/adapters.js:327-331 comments "`inputs` is the complete binding map; `declared_consumes` mirrors the producing runtime's own notion of a declared Part read, which in pyto omits `fn:` result refs (pcr.py:120 Receipt.declared_consumes). Read both so the index is the same whichever convention a producer follows", and viewer/test/record_schema.py:280 does the same union. Neither validator enforces the sentence, so the suites are green while the contract text is false. A third reader written from RECORD.md alone would derive parts[].read_by with 6 readers missing (every scratch.ablation.model.* would show read_by []), which is exactly what my first independent re-derivation produced before I switched to reading `inputs`. This is a shared-contract clause, so it is not a pyto-local matter: it is the sentence the JS runtime is also held to.
findings.required_fix: Amend RECORD.md:52-54 to state what both runtimes actually do (no code change needed, and none is possible in pcr.py): `inputs` is the complete binding map in testimony spelling; `declared_consumes` carries the producing runtime's declared Part reads only -- the `px:` bindings -- so it is empty where every binding is a `fn:` result ref (pyto: pcr.py:120 Receipt.declared_consumes; DiscStudio has only px: bindings, so there the two coincide). Add the one-line consequence readers depend on: a part index must union `inputs` and `declared_consumes` and resolve `fn:<id>` through that invocation's `into` (adapters.js:327-331, record_schema.py:280). Include a second worked invocation in the RECORD.md example that has an `fn:` binding, so the example itself disambiguates. Note the RECORD.md edit in the CHANGES.md Day 3 entry.

findings.claim: The build report's findings describe a tree that no longer exists, and one finding asserts the OPPOSITE of the shipped behaviour. It claims: "Without observe=True the record is still emitted with every observed-only field null ... Pinned by DayOneRecord::test_without_observe_the_observed_fields_are_null_not_guessed."
findings.evidence: The shipped code refuses instead: materialize.py:322-337 raises ValueError ("run_record needs the receipts of the run it describes ... Call PCR.run(pxc, observe=True)"), documented at materialize.py:16-17 and CHANGES.md:660-673 ("A receipt-less run emitted a document tagged with a schema it did not satisfy ... The null-emitting branch is gone rather than dead"). The test is named test_without_observe_run_record_refuses_instead_of_emitting_nulls (test_materialize.py:253); the test the report names does not exist (`grep -n "the_observed_fields_are_null" tests/test_materialize.py` -> no match). The same round also edited the shared contract -- pyto/viewer/RECORD.md:73 now reads "`PcrRun.receipts` -- required, so `PCR.run(pxc, observe=True)`" (was "when `observe=True`") -- and the build report does not mention that edit at all. Three further staleness points: materialize.py is 661 lines, not the reported 580; the reported line anchors are all off (SCHEMA is at :47 not :45, render_value at :179 not :128, run_record at :281 not :212, write_record at :479 not :407, tick_sheets at :604 not :523); and the reported output_tail counts (library 93, grouped-ablation 211, viewer 71, eight suites) are stale against my run (library 103, grouped-ablation 230, viewer 83, plus a ninth suite viewer-record-schema 19).
findings.required_fix: Regenerate the build report from the tree that is actually on disk: correct the observe=False finding to state the refusal (materialize.py:322-337) and name test_materialize.py:253, add the RECORD.md:73 contract edit as its own reported change, refresh the line anchors and the file length, and paste the current check_all.sh tail (nine suites). A handoff report whose headline finding is the inverse of the code is worse than no report.

findings.claim: The report's finding that the one out-of-scope file changed only in `_snapshot` and that "No test count, expectation or assertion changed" is false.
findings.evidence: `git diff 83422cf -- pyto/experiments/grouped-ablation/test_grouped_ablation.py` shows +73/-19 across three sites: _snapshot was rewritten to os.walk (as reported, now at :401-418); test_commit_txt_... was RENAMED (…watched_paths_changed -> …watched_code_changed) and its assertions CHANGED from `commit_sha()`/`dirty_paths()` to `commit_sha(exclude=excludes)`/`dirty_paths(exclude=evidence_excludes())`; and two whole new tests were added (test_evidence_excludes_names_the_evidence_tree_and_nothing_else, test_a_dirty_producing_file_still_stamps_dirty_with_the_evidence_excluded), which is why the suite moved 211 -> 230 rather than staying put. New imports EVIDENCE_ROOT and evidence_excludes come from run.py, so run.py grew a public helper too.
findings.required_fix: State the full extent of the change to this file in the report and in CHANGES.md: the renamed test, the relaxed-but-re-pinned dirty-stamp assertions (evidence excluded, producing code still dirt), and the two added tests. Keep the claim "no assertion was weakened" only if it is stated as what it is -- the exclusion is narrowed to evidence/ and a companion test proves an uncommitted code edit still stamps -dirty.

findings.claim: `run_record` lets a caller inject an arbitrary key into `source`, silently producing a document that both readers reject.
findings.evidence: materialize.py:461-463 builds `document_source = {"runtime", "version", "commit"}` then `document_source.update(source)` with no key check, and run_record never validates its own output. viewer/test/record_schema.py:38 SOURCE_KEYS and viewer/adapters.js validate are exact key sets in both directions (RECORD.md:65, "missing fields are null, never invented"), so `run_record(..., source={"branch": "x"})` writes a file that fails at `source` on both sides -- at write_record time, not at call time. The one in-tree caller (materialize_run.py:60) passes only runtime/commit, so nothing is broken today; none of the 39 tests in tests/test_materialize.py covers a source override with an unknown key.
findings.required_fix: Restrict the update to the three RECORD.md source keys and raise ValueError naming the offending key otherwise (the same shape as the receipt-less refusal at materialize.py:322-337), with a test that pins the refusal.

findings.claim: On the sheets, the `reads` line is blank for 13 of the 15 invocations, so the picture under-reports what each Calculation consumed — the founding question of the day.
findings.evidence: _invocation_lines:517 sets `reads = invocation["actual_consumes"]` and only falls back to `inputs` when it is None, never when it is []. Because pcr.py rewrites a Part binding into a ResultRef, every fit/score/compare invocation has actual_consumes [], so tick-002-Score.png prints `reads   -` on all six panels even though each consumed a model and the split (visible in the rendered PNG I read). The information is not lost -- the `inputs` line above shows {'model': 'fn:fit.all', 'split': 'fn:split'} -- but the record's own parts[].read_by does count those reads (record.json: scratch.ablation.model.all read_by ['score.all']), so the sheet is less informative than the record it renders.
findings.required_fix: Fall back to the `fn:`-resolved read set when actual_consumes is empty as well as when it is None -- i.e. render the same reads the part index derives (inputs resolved through into_by_id) -- or label the line `reads (store)` so a blank one reads as "nothing came off the store" rather than "nothing was read".
